content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-17
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline): Show all of the user's entries in a timeline, whatever their origin, with a per-entry synchronization badge, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF07) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros' (default) and 'Tela 4 — Vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.4); the 'Sessão expirada' overlay (section 4). Badge semantics: docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md. Backend: GET /entries, GET /entries/:id, GET /auth/session, POST /auth/refresh. Depends on F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-17
14	
15	- Q: RF01 (already delivered) opens the Insertion Modal only from Home/Chat's "+" button and, on a successful save, always returns the user to Home/Chat. This unit adds a second entry point — the "Criar primeiro registro" action on this screen's empty state — so where should a save started from there return the user to, and must the newly created entry appear here immediately? → A: It returns to this screen (Meus Registros), not to Home/Chat, and the newly created entry appears immediately in its correct date group. The entire purpose of the empty-state action is to take the user from zero entries to seeing their first one; returning them to Home/Chat instead would leave the empty state looking unresolved even though the entry was created. This reuses the same in-memory entries store RF01 already appends to on a successful save (and that it documented as existing "for later units ... to read"), merged with whatever this screen has already loaded from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: `GET /entries/:id` is listed under this requirement, but no entry-detail or full-text screen appears anywhere in the prototype's navigation map or navigable-state catalog for "Meus Registros" — only a card with a truncated text excerpt. What is this endpoint actually for in this unit? → A: It is not used to open a detail view (none is drawn anywhere, and inventing one would conflict with this unit's visual-fidelity obligation to the frozen prototype). Instead, this unit uses it to re-confirm the state of one specific, already-loaded entry during reconciliation — for example, after the "Sessão expirada" overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed — rather than re-fetching the entire paginated list, which is what keeps already-rendered cards and the scroll position from being disturbed, in line with this requirement's own acceptance criterion about not losing scroll position. This unit's own scope never actually produces a locally-pending or unreconciled entry (every entry rendered here is already server-confirmed, per the Assumption on badge states below), so no reconciliation trigger exists to wire `GET /entries/:id` into — it is implemented and tested as a documented repository capability for a future unit's use, not called from anywhere in this unit's own code. See plan.md's Post-Design Constitution Check (research.md R7) for the design-time confirmation of this. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17	- Q: When this screen merges the entry RF01's save flow already placed in the app's local in-memory entries store with the entries this screen fetches from the backend, how should it avoid showing that same entry twice? → A: Dedupe by entry ID. RF01's save flow only adds an entry to the local store after the backend has confirmed the write, so every locally-held entry already carries a real, server-issued ID; when a fetched backend page returns an entry whose ID already exists in the local store, the two are recognized as the same entry and shown once (preferring the freshly-fetched copy's confirmation data — `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` — since it is at least as current as the local one). This is the simplest reliable key available and is what keeps SC-001's "100% of entries appear exactly once" true once a locally-created entry's page is later re-fetched from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	- Q: Within each date group (and across date groups), in what order are entries displayed — and does that order match the order newer pages get appended to older ones while scrolling? → A: Reverse-chronological throughout: date groups run newest-to-oldest ("Hoje" at the very top), and within each group entries run newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time. This matches the backend's cursor-based pagination (each further page is strictly older than what's already loaded) and the prototype's own "Hoje"/"Ontem"/older-dates ordering, and it is the only ordering under which "scrolling down loads older entries, appended at the bottom" (FR-003, Edge Cases) is coherent without resorting already-rendered cards. Neither the prototype extract nor `requirements.md` states this explicitly, so this is a reasonable technical decision per Constitution Principle I rather than an invented behavior with no basis in the frozen inputs. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
19	
20	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
21	
22	### User Story 1 - Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of how it was created (Priority: P1)
23	
24	A user who has written notes, recorded audio, and captured photos over several days opens "Meus Registros" from the side menu and sees all of those entries together, in a single timeline, grouped by the day they happened ("Hoje", "Ontem", then calendar dates), each one visually marked with where it came from.
25	
26	**Why this priority**: This is the entire reason the screen exists — a user's journal is split across capture methods, and without this unified view there is no way to look back at everything they've recorded.
27	
28	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding a user with entries of different origins across different days, opening "Meus Registros", and confirming every entry appears exactly once, grouped under the correct date heading, with an origin-appropriate visual marker on each.
29	
30	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
31	
32	1. **Given** a user with entries created as text, audio, and photo on different days, **When** they open "Meus Registros", **Then** every one of those entries appears in the list, grouped under date headings ("Hoje" for today's entries, "Ontem" for yesterday's, an explicit date for anything older), each showing a time, an origin-colored marker and icon, a text excerpt, and a synchronization badge.
33	2. **Given** an entry that has tags attached (from existing account data), **When** its card is rendered, **Then** those tags appear as read-only chips on the card; **given** an entry with no tags, **When** its card is rendered, **Then** no tag chips appear for it.
34	3. **Given** the list of entries is longer than fits on screen, **When** the user scrolls down, **Then** older entries load automatically and are appended to the list without disturbing the entries already shown or losing the user's scroll position.
35	
36	---
37	
38	### User Story 2 - Starting from nothing (Priority: P1)
39	
40	A brand-new user, or one who has not yet created any entry, opens "Meus Registros" and sees a clear empty state instead of a blank or broken screen, with a direct path to creating their first entry.
41	
42	**Why this priority**: Equally fundamental to Story 1 — this screen must handle the zero-entries case correctly from day one, since it is the state every account starts in.
43	
44	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening "Meus Registros" on an account with zero entries, confirming the empty-state illustration, message, and call-to-action appear, and confirming that action leads to creating an entry that then populates the screen.
45	
46	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
47	
48	1. **Given** an account with no entries at all, **When** the user opens "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the empty state — a notebook illustration, the message "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action — instead of an empty list.
49	2. **Given** the empty state is showing, **When** the user taps "Criar primeiro registro", **Then** the existing entry-creation flow opens; **when** they complete a save, **Then** they return to "Meus Registros" and see that new entry now populating the list in place of the empty state.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - The session expires while browsing (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A user is scrolled partway through their history when their backend session expires. A clear prompt to log in again appears over the screen, and once they do, they land back exactly where they were — same entries loaded, same scroll position.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: An edge condition of Story 1 that protects against data loss and disorientation; it cannot be exercised until the timeline itself exists, but it is important enough to this requirement's own acceptance criteria to rank above cosmetic concerns.
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading the timeline, scrolling to a known position, forcing a session-expired response, confirming the overlay appears without resetting the list, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact scroll position and content.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** the user is scrolled to a particular position in "Meus Registros", **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** the "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the screen without discarding the loaded entries or resetting the scroll position.
64	2. **Given** the overlay is visible, **When** the user re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay dismisses and the screen is restored exactly as it was, without reloading or reordering the entries already on screen.
65	
66	---
67

69	
70	While a user is looking at their timeline — including while a session renewal is happening in the background, or while the "Sessão expirada" overlay is up — each entry's synchronization badge keeps showing an accurate state (synchronized, synchronizing, or sync error) and is never frozen, blanked, or delayed by whatever is happening with the session.
71	
72	**Why this priority**: A correctness and trust property layered on top of Story 1's display rather than a feature of its own; it depends on the timeline and the session-expiry handling of Story 3 already existing.
73	
74	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by putting entries in each of the three badge states, forcing a session expiration and renewal in the background, and confirming every badge's state is unaffected by that session activity throughout.
75	
76	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
77

81	---
82	
83	### Edge Cases
84	
85	- The device is offline while viewing this screen: already-loaded entries remain visible and scrollable (per the product's offline behavior), but loading further pages fails with a clear, retryable message instead of hanging or crashing; no write of any kind happens from this screen.
86	- The backend returns an entry whose origin is `chat` — a source this app cannot yet produce (chat and "save to journal" are later units) but that `GET /entries` can still return (e.g., from seed/test data): the card renders with the origin's defined marker and icon like any other, without erroring or treating it as unrecognized.
87	- The most recent page of entries is itself empty (e.g., nothing happened today or yesterday) while the account has entries further back: paging continues to load those older groups rather than showing the empty state, which is reserved for a true zero-entries account.
88	- A page load fails outright (not just going offline mid-session): the user sees a clear, retryable loading error for that page without losing or corrupting the entries already shown above it.

90	
91	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
92	
93	### Functional Requirements
94	
95	- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a "Meus Registros" screen, reachable from the app's existing side-menu navigation, that fetches and displays all of the signed-in user's journal entries regardless of origin (manual, audio, photo, or chat).

100	- **FR-006**: Loading or refreshing this screen's data MUST check the session and silently renew it when merely expired-but-renewable, without interrupting the user, consistent with the app's existing session-renewal behavior.

Reconciling any single entry's state after such an event (or after any other interruption) MUST be done by re-confirming that specific entry rather than by reloading or reordering the whole list.
102	- **FR-008**: The screen's header download affordance and its search bar with funnel button MUST be rendered to match the prototype for visual fidelity, but MUST NOT perform export or search/filter behavior in this unit — those behaviors belong to later units and MUST NOT be implemented here.
103	- **FR-009**: While the device is offline, entries already loaded on this screen MUST remain visible and scrollable; attempting to load further pages MUST fail with a clear, retryable message rather than hanging or crashing, and no write of any kind MUST be attempted from this screen.
104	- **FR-010**: This unit MUST NOT implement entry search, text filtering, the category/date/type filter sheet, active-filter chips, export generation, or any other behavior reserved for a later unit (RF05, RF06, or any later RF) or for an extension feature (requirements section 2).
105	- **FR-011**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration in any way.
106	
107	### Key Entities
108	
109	- **Journal Entry**: The same persisted, immutable record introduced by RF01 — text content, a creation/occurrence time, and an origin — now also carrying the server-confirmation data (its last-confirmed-write time and the ever-increasing revision counter) and any read-only tags attached to it, and now rendered regardless of which of the four possible origins (`manual`, `audio`, `photo`, `chat`) produced it.
110	- **Synchronization Badge State**: A derived, per-entry value — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed entirely on the device from an entry's own confirmation data and the device's own record of any write for that entry still pending or unreconciled; never itself stored by or requested directly from the backend.
111	- **Entry Timeline Page**: The windowed view of the user's full entry history currently loaded on screen — the entries fetched so far and the position to continue from — preserved across scrolling, backgrounding, and a session expiration/renewal cycle so the user's place is never lost.
112	
113	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
114	
115	### Measurable Outcomes
116	
117	- **SC-001**: 100% of a user's entries — across every origin they've used — appear exactly once in the timeline (including an entry created via this screen's own empty-state flow that a later backend fetch also returns, de-duplicated by entry ID), correctly grouped by the day they occurred, with no entry requiring the user to know or remember which capture method created it.

119	- **SC-003**: Users can scroll through their entire entry history, however long, with additional entries loading automatically in every case, without ever needing a manual "load more" action or losing their scroll position.

121	- **SC-005**: Every entry visible on screen shows one of the three defined synchronization states at all times, unaffected by whatever is happening with the user's session at that moment.
122	
123	## Assumptions
124	
125	- The header's download icon and the search bar with its funnel button are rendered to match the prototype (visual fidelity) but are inert placeholders in this unit; their behavior belongs to RF05 (export) and RF06 (search/filter), both later in the delivery order.

# Feature Specification: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)

**Feature Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-17

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline): Show all of the user's entries in a timeline, whatever their origin, with a per-entry synchronization badge, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF07) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros' (default) and 'Tela 4 — Vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.4); the 'Sessão expirada' overlay (section 4). Badge semantics: docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md. Backend: GET /entries, GET /entries/:id, GET /auth/session, POST /auth/refresh. Depends on F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-17

- Q: RF01 (already delivered) opens the Insertion Modal only from Home/Chat's "+" button and, on a successful save, always returns the user to Home/Chat. This unit adds a second entry point — the "Criar primeiro registro" action on this screen's empty state — so where should a save started from there return the user to, and must the newly created entry appear here immediately? → A: It returns to this screen (Meus Registros), not to Home/Chat, and the newly created entry appears immediately in its correct date group. The entire purpose of the empty-state action is to take the user from zero entries to seeing their first one; returning them to Home/Chat instead would leave the empty state looking unresolved even though the entry was created. This reuses the same in-memory entries store RF01 already appends to on a successful save (and that it documented as existing "for later units ... to read"), merged with whatever this screen has already loaded from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `GET /entries/:id` is listed under this requirement, but no entry-detail or full-text screen appears anywhere in the prototype's navigation map or navigable-state catalog for "Meus Registros" — only a card with a truncated text excerpt. What is this endpoint actually for in this unit? → A: It is not used to open a detail view (none is drawn anywhere, and inventing one would conflict with this unit's visual-fidelity obligation to the frozen prototype). Instead, this unit uses it to re-confirm the state of one specific, already-loaded entry during reconciliation — for example, after the "Sessão expirada" overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed — rather than re-fetching the entire paginated list, which is what keeps already-rendered cards and the scroll position from being disturbed, in line with this requirement's own acceptance criterion about not losing scroll position. This unit's own scope never actually produces a locally-pending or unreconciled entry (every entry rendered here is already server-confirmed, per the Assumption on badge states below), so no reconciliation trigger exists to wire `GET /entries/:id` into — it is implemented and tested as a documented repository capability for a future unit's use, not called from anywhere in this unit's own code. See plan.md's Post-Design Constitution Check (research.md R7) for the design-time confirmation of this. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: When this screen merges the entry RF01's save flow already placed in the app's local in-memory entries store with the entries this screen fetches from the backend, how should it avoid showing that same entry twice? → A: Dedupe by entry ID. RF01's save flow only adds an entry to the local store after the backend has confirmed the write, so every locally-held entry already carries a real, server-issued ID; when a fetched backend page returns an entry whose ID already exists in the local store, the two are recognized as the same entry and shown once (preferring the freshly-fetched copy's confirmation data — `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` — since it is at least as current as the local one). This is the simplest reliable key available and is what keeps SC-001's "100% of entries appear exactly once" true once a locally-created entry's page is later re-fetched from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: Within each date group (and across date groups), in what order are entries displayed — and does that order match the order newer pages get appended to older ones while scrolling? → A: Reverse-chronological throughout: date groups run newest-to-oldest ("Hoje" at the very top), and within each group entries run newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time. This matches the backend's cursor-based pagination (each further page is strictly older than what's already loaded) and the prototype's own "Hoje"/"Ontem"/older-dates ordering, and it is the only ordering under which "scrolling down loads older entries, appended at the bottom" (FR-003, Edge Cases) is coherent without resorting already-rendered cards. Neither the prototype extract nor `requirements.md` states this explicitly, so this is a reasonable technical decision per Constitution Principle I rather than an invented behavior with no basis in the frozen inputs. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of how it was created (Priority: P1)

A user who has written notes, recorded audio, and captured photos over several days opens "Meus Registros" from the side menu and sees all of those entries together, in a single timeline, grouped by the day they happened ("Hoje", "Ontem", then calendar dates), each one visually marked with where it came from.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding a user with entries of different origins across different days, opening "Meus Registros", and confirming every entry appears exactly once, grouped under the correct date heading, with an origin-appropriate visual marker on each.

1. **Given** a user with entries created as text, audio, and photo on different days, **When** they open "Meus Registros", **Then** every one of those entries appears in the list, grouped under date headings ("Hoje" for today's entries, "Ontem" for yesterday's, an explicit date for anything older), each showing a time, an origin-colored marker and icon, a text excerpt, and a synchronization badge.
2. **Given** an entry that has tags attached (from existing account data), **When** its card is rendered, **Then** those tags appear as read-only chips on the card; **given** an entry with no tags, **When** its card is rendered, **Then** no tag chips appear for it.
3. **Given** the list of entries is longer than fits on screen, **When** the user scrolls down, **Then** older entries load automatically and are appended to the list without disturbing the entries already shown or losing the user's scroll position.

---

### User Story 2 - Starting from nothing (Priority: P1)

A brand-new user, or one who has not yet created any entry, opens "Meus Registros" and sees a clear empty state instead of a blank or broken screen, with a direct path to creating their first entry.

2. **Given** the empty state is showing, **When** the user taps "Criar primeiro registro", **Then** the existing entry-creation flow opens; **when** they complete a save, **Then** they return to "Meus Registros" and see that new entry now populating the list in place of the empty state.

---

### User Story 3 - The session expires while browsing (Priority: P2)

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** entries in each of the three synchronization states, **When** a session renewal happens silently in the background, **Then** every badge still reflects its correct, unchanged state throughout and after the renewal.
2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible over the timeline, **When** the user inspects the cards underneath (e.g., once it is dismissed), **Then** every badge's state is exactly what it was before the overlay appeared, with no badge having changed, frozen, or disappeared because of the session event.

---

### Edge Cases

- The device is offline while viewing this screen: already-loaded entries remain visible and scrollable (per the product's offline behavior), but loading further pages fails with a clear, retryable message instead of hanging or crashing; no write of any kind happens from this screen.

- Date-heading grouping ("Hoje", "Ontem", explicit dates) uses the device's local calendar day applied to each entry's occurrence timestamp, matching the prototype's labels.

- "No BLoC imports another BLoC directly" (the requirement's own architecture-level acceptance criterion) is carried forward as an implementation-time constraint for the planning phase; at the specification level it is expressed through FR-005's and FR-007's independence requirements between the synchronization badge and session/authentication handling.

  (never a bloc) being the thing that reads one feature's bloc stream and dispatches into another's.

  immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id`") and found it still holds: nothing in
  this design ever produces a locally-pending/failed write for an entry this unit can display, so no
  reconciliation trigger exists to wire up — confirmed not an oversight, documented as a deliberate, narrow
  scope boundary. This resolves spec.md Clarification 2's own illustrative example ("after the Sessão
  expirada overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed") as a description of `getById()`'s intended
  future purpose, not a call site this unit implements.
- No change surfaces that touches `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any native iOS project file,
  or any AI provider — Principle III remains intact.

No new violations. Gate remains PASS.

# Tasks: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. RNF07 (`lib/**/domain/**` ≥80% coverage) is carried into this unit's Constitution
Check as "PASS (gate carried into tasks)", and both `contracts/entries-repository-extension.md` and
`contracts/records-bloc.md` each define an explicit scenario table "for `/speckit-tasks` to
schedule" — so test tasks are generated alongside implementation, matching RF01/RF02/RF03's existing
`bloc_test`/`mocktail` style exactly.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (US1–US4, spec.md priorities P1/P1/P2/P3). Per
contracts/records-bloc.md, `RecordsBloc` and `RecordsPage` are each extended incrementally across
several stories (same convention RF02's own tasks.md used for the shared `InsertionModalBloc`) — "independent" here means each story's acceptance scenarios can be exercised and automated-tested on
their own once the prior stories it builds on exist, not that each story gets its own bloc or page.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1 (seeing every entry, regardless of origin), US2 (starting from nothing /
  empty state), US3 (session expires while browsing), US4 (the sync badge tells the truth during
  session trouble)

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project (F000/RF01/RF03's existing `lib/`, `test/`) — see plan.md Project Structure.
This unit fills in the already-existing `lib/features/records/` placeholder feature folder and
extends `lib/features/entries/`, `lib/core/network/`, `lib/core/di/`, `lib/core/routing/`, and
`lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/` in place; no new top-level directory.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

**Purpose**: Project initialization — N/A for this unit.

No setup tasks apply. This unit adds no new package, no native-project change, and no new `.env`
variable — it reuses the full existing stack as-is (plan.md Technical Context, Primary
Dependencies: "No additions"; research.md R9 explicitly rejects adding `intl`). Proceed directly to
Foundational.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The `entries/` extensions every story's data ultimately flows through
(`ApiClient.queryParameters`, `EntrySource.chat`, `EntriesPage`, `EntriesRepository.list()`/
`.getById()` with silent-refresh-and-retry), plus the three pure `records/domain/` helpers
(`SyncBadge`, `DateGrouper`, `EntryMerger`) every story's presentation layer calls. No UI exists yet
after this phase — `RecordsBloc`/`RecordsPage` are built starting in User Story 1.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No tasks — proceed directly to Foundational.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: No dependencies — BLOCKS all user stories.
- **User Stories (Phase 3–6)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
  - US1 (P1) builds the core `RecordsBloc`/`RecordsPage`/widgets and is this unit's MVP.
  - US2 (P1) extends `RecordsBloc` (`_onLocalCacheRefreshed`) and `RecordsPage` (the empty-state
    branch) built in US1 — depends on US1's T019/T023 already existing.
  - US3 (P2) extends `RecordsPage` (the `reauthRequired` subscription) built in US1/US2 — depends on
    US1's T023 and US2's T031 (same file) already existing. `RecordsBloc`'s own `AuthExpiredFailure`
    branching was already built correctly in US1's T019; US3 adds the widget-level wiring plus the
    tests that specifically exercise it.
  - US4 (P3) depends on US3's `AuthExpiredFailure` test fixtures (T035) to build its own
    badge-independence assertion against, and on US3's overlay wiring (T033) for its manual
    verification step.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: Depends on all four stories being complete.

### Within Each User Story

- Events/state additions before the bloc handler that needs them; the bloc handler before the DI
  registration that constructs it; DI before the page that reads it via `context.read<RecordsBloc>()`.
- Tests are written alongside (and can run immediately after) each handler task, extending one
  shared `records_bloc_test.dart` across stories — the same convention RF02's own tasks.md used for
  `insertion_modal_bloc_test.dart`.
- Story complete (events/state + bloc handlers + widgets + DI/routing + tests) before moving to the
  next priority.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T001, T002, T003 (Foundational `entries/` plumbing) in parallel with each other; T011, T013, T015
  (Foundational `records/domain/` helpers) in parallel with each other and with T001–T003 — all
  different files.

  implementation tasks land.
- T012, T014, T016 (pure-helper tests) in parallel with each other once T011/T013/T015 land.
- T017/T018 (US1 event/state files) in parallel with each other; T021/T022 (US1 widgets) in parallel

1. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks all stories).
2. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.
3. **STOP and VALIDATE**: open "Meus Registros" on a seeded account, confirm every entry appears
   exactly once grouped by date with the right origin marker/badge/excerpt/tags, and confirm
   scrolling to the bottom loads and appends further pages without disturbing what's on screen.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Foundational → `EntriesRepository.list()`/`.getById()` and the three pure `records/domain/`
   helpers exist; nothing visible changes yet.
2. Add US1 → "Meus Registros" works end to end for an account with entries (SC-001, SC-003).
3. Add US2 → a zero-entries account sees the empty state and can create its first entry from it
   (SC-002).
4. Add US3 → a session expiring mid-browse surfaces the overlay without data loss (SC-004).
5. Add US4 → the sync badge's session-independence property is explicitly verified (SC-005).
6. Polish → RNF06/RNF07 gates + quickstart's full manual pass.

---

## Notes

- `records_bloc.dart` and `records_page.dart` are each touched by multiple story phases
  (T019/T020/T030 for the bloc; T023/T031/T033 for the page) — this mirrors RF02's own tasks.md
  precedent: a deliberate consequence of one shared bloc/page serving the whole screen, not a
  same-file conflict to avoid.
- `records_placeholder_page.dart` is deleted only in T026 (US1), once `AppRoutes.records` no longer
  references it (T024) — the app must keep compiling at every checkpoint.
- No task in this list touches `docs/input/`, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any
  native iOS project file, or any RF04–RF10/extension-feature behavior — all explicitly out of scope
  (FR-010, FR-011).
- `EntriesRepository.getById()` is implemented and tested (T005, T006, T008, T009) but has no call
  site anywhere in this task list, by design (research.md R7) — nothing in this unit ever produces a
  locally-pending/unreconciled entry for it to reconcile.
- Every color `record_card.dart`/`sync_badge_dot.dart` render (T021, T022) already exists in
  `DesignTokens` — no task in this list adds a new design token (plan.md Constraints, Principle
  IV/RNF08).

1	# Contract: `EntriesRepository` extension (`lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`)
2	
3	Extends the interface `specs/003-multimodal-capture/contracts/entries-repository.md` already defines
4	(`create`, `cachedEntries`, both unchanged) with the two read methods this unit needs. Still the single seam
5	every feature reading or writing entries depends on — `records/` is simply its first reader.
6	
7	```dart
8	abstract class EntriesRepository {
9	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source}); // unchanged
10	  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                   // unchanged
11	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor});
12	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
13	}
14	```
15	
16	## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` (orchestration, data layer)
17	
18	```dart
19	Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) async {
20	  final result = await _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor);
21	  return result.match(
22	    (failure) => failure is AuthExpiredFailure
23	        ? await _retryAfterSilentRefresh(() => _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor))
24	        : Left(failure),
25	    (page) => Right(page),
26	  );
27	}
28	```
29	
30	## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.getById()` (orchestration, data layer)
31	
32	Identical shape, over `_remoteDataSource.getById(id)` instead.
33	
34	## The shared retry helper (private to `EntriesRepositoryImpl`)
35	
36	```dart
37	Future<Either<Failure, T>> _retryAfterSilentRefresh<T>(
38	  Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function() retry,
39	) async {
40	  final refreshed = await _sessionRepository.refresh();
41	  return refreshed.match(
42	    (_) => Left(const AuthExpiredFailure(message: 'Session could not be renewed', requestId: '')),
43	    (_) => retry(),   // exactly one retry — no loop, no second refresh attempt
44	  );
45	}
46	```
47	
48	- **Exactly one retry.** If the retried call *also* comes back `AuthExpiredFailure` (a pathological
49	  double-expiry), it is returned to the caller as-is — no second refresh attempt, no loop. This is a
50	  deliberately simple, bounded policy; nothing in spec.md requires more.
51	- **The `Left` branch always normalizes to a fresh `AuthExpiredFailure`**, regardless of what the refresh
52	  attempt itself failed with (`AuthInvalidFailure` for no stored refresh token, or whatever `/auth/refresh`
53	  itself returned) — callers (`RecordsBloc`) only ever need to know "could not be silently renewed," not the
54	  refresh call's own internal failure shape, mirroring how `CheckSessionUseCase` (specs/001) already
55	  normalizes every unrenewable-session case down to one outcome rather than leaking the refresh call's raw
56	  failure type upward.
57	- **`create()` is untouched** — out of this unit's scope (research.md R4).
58	
59	## `EntriesRemoteDataSource` additions (data layer)
60	
61	```dart
62	Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) {
63	  return _apiClient
64	      .call('entries-list', method: 'GET', queryParameters: cursor == null ? null : {'cursor': cursor})
65	      .flatMap(_parseEntriesPage);
66	}
67	
68	Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id) {
69	  return _apiClient
70	      .call('entries-get', method: 'GET', pathSegments: [id])
71	      .flatMap(_parseEntry);   // the same private parser create() already uses
72	}
73	```
74	
75	- `_parseEntry` (existing, `create()`'s private parser) is reused verbatim for a single object; a new
76	  `_parseEntriesPage` parses `data` (a list, each element through the same per-entry field logic `_parseEntry`
77	  already has — factored so neither duplicates the other) and `meta.nextCursor`.
78	- Malformed-response parsing failures (`TypeError`/`FormatException`) map to `ValidationFailure`, exactly like
79	  `create()`'s existing `_parseEntry` catch clauses — no new failure-mapping behavior.
80	
81	## `ApiClient.call()` (core layer) — `queryParameters` addition
82	
83	```dart
84	Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
85	  String function, {
86	  required String method,
87	  Map<String, dynamic>? body,
88	  List<String>? pathSegments,
89	  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
90	  AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession,
91	}) async {
92	  // ...unchanged URL-building...
93	  final response = await _dio.request<Map<String, dynamic>>(
94	    url,
95	    data: body,
96	    queryParameters: queryParameters,   // NEW — passed straight through to dio
97	    options: Options(method: method, headers: {...}),
98	  );
99	  // ...unchanged response handling...
100	}
101	```
102	
103	Every existing call site (`entries-create`, `auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) omits the new
104	parameter and is byte-for-byte unaffected.
105	
106	## Who depends on this
107

# Contract: `EntriesRepository` extension (`lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`)

Extends the interface `specs/003-multimodal-capture/contracts/entries-repository.md` already defines
(`create`, `cachedEntries`, both unchanged) with the two read methods this unit needs. Still the single seam
every feature reading or writing entries depends on — `records/` is simply its first reader.

```dart
abstract class EntriesRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source}); // unchanged
  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                   // unchanged
  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor});
  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
}
```

## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` (orchestration, data layer)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) async {
  final result = await _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor);
  return result.match(
    (failure) => failure is AuthExpiredFailure
        ? await _retryAfterSilentRefresh(() => _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor))
        : Left(failure),
    (page) => Right(page),
  );
}
```

## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.getById()` (orchestration, data layer)

Identical shape, over `_remoteDataSource.getById(id)` instead.

## The shared retry helper (private to `EntriesRepositoryImpl`)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, T>> _retryAfterSilentRefresh<T>(
  Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function() retry,
) async {
  final refreshed = await _sessionRepository.refresh();
  return refreshed.match(
    (_) => Left(const AuthExpiredFailure(message: 'Session could not be renewed', requestId: '')),
    (_) => retry(),   // exactly one retry — no loop, no second refresh attempt
  );
}
```

- **Exactly one retry.** If the retried call *also* comes back `AuthExpiredFailure` (a pathological
  double-expiry), it is returned to the caller as-is — no second refresh attempt, no loop. This is a
  deliberately simple, bounded policy; nothing in spec.md requires more.
- **The `Left` branch always normalizes to a fresh `AuthExpiredFailure`**, regardless of what the refresh
  attempt itself failed with (`AuthInvalidFailure` for no stored refresh token, or whatever `/auth/refresh`
  itself returned) — callers (`RecordsBloc`) only ever need to know "could not be silently renewed," not the
  refresh call's own internal failure shape, mirroring how `CheckSessionUseCase` (specs/001) already
  normalizes every unrenewable-session case down to one outcome rather than leaking the refresh call's raw
  failure type upward.
- **`create()` is untouched** — out of this unit's scope (research.md R4).

## `EntriesRemoteDataSource` additions (data layer)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) {
  return _apiClient
      .call('entries-list', method: 'GET', queryParameters: cursor == null ? null : {'cursor': cursor})
      .flatMap(_parseEntriesPage);
}

Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id) {
  return _apiClient
      .call('entries-get', method: 'GET', pathSegments: [id])
      .flatMap(_parseEntry);   // the same private parser create() already uses
}
```

- `_parseEntry` (existing, `create()`'s private parser) is reused verbatim for a single object; a new
  `_parseEntriesPage` parses `data` (a list, each element through the same per-entry field logic `_parseEntry`
  already has — factored so neither duplicates the other) and `meta.nextCursor`.
- Malformed-response parsing failures (`TypeError`/`FormatException`) map to `ValidationFailure`, exactly like
  `create()`'s existing `_parseEntry` catch clauses — no new failure-mapping behavior.

## `ApiClient.call()` (core layer) — `queryParameters` addition

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
  String function, {
  required String method,
  Map<String, dynamic>? body,
  List<String>? pathSegments,
  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
  AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession,
}) async {
  // ...unchanged URL-building...
  final response = await _dio.request<Map<String, dynamic>>(
    url,
    data: body,
    queryParameters: queryParameters,   // NEW — passed straight through to dio
    options: Options(method: method, headers: {...}),
  );
  // ...unchanged response handling...
}
```

Every existing call site (`entries-create`, `auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) omits the new
parameter and is byte-for-byte unaffected.

## Who depends on this

`RecordsBloc` (`list`/`getById`, via `EntriesRepository` only — never `EntriesRemoteDataSource`/`ApiClient`
directly, same layering every existing feature already observes). No other unit yet calls `list()`/`getById()`
— RF06 (semantic search) is the next likely caller, reusing the same silent-refresh-and-retry behavior for
free.

## Test scenarios this contract owns (RNF07/RNF09 — for `/speckit-tasks` to schedule, not built here)

| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `list()` succeeds on the first attempt | `Right(EntriesPage(...))`, no refresh call made |
| 2 | `list()` fails `AuthExpiredFailure`, refresh succeeds, retry succeeds | `Right(EntriesPage(...))`, exactly 2 remote calls + 1 refresh call |
| 3 | `list()` fails `AuthExpiredFailure`, refresh itself fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, no second refresh attempt |
| 4 | `list()` fails any other code (timeout/offline/validation/...) | `Left(<that failure>)` unchanged, no refresh attempted |
| 5 | `getById()` — same 4 scenarios as `list()` | same shapes |
| 6 | `list(cursor: 'abc')` | `ApiClient.call` receives `queryParameters: {'cursor': 'abc'}` |
| 7 | `list()` (no cursor) | `ApiClient.call` receives `queryParameters: null` |
| 8 | Response containing a `chat`-sourced entry | Parses without throwing, `EntrySource.chat` |

33	  const EntriesPage({required this.entries, required this.nextCursor});
34	  final List<Entry> entries;
35	  final String? nextCursor;
36	}

38	
39	## `EntriesRepository` — extended (`lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`)
40	
41	```dart
42	abstract class EntriesRepository {
43	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source}); // unchanged (RF01)
44	  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                   // unchanged (RF01)
45	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor});                                      // NEW
46	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);                                                // NEW
47	}

49	
50	- **`list`** → `GET /entries` (`entries-list`), query parameters `cursor` (when non-null) only — no `limit`
51	  override (backend default 20), no `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (filters are RF06's).
52	- **`getById`** → `GET /entries/:id` (`entries-get`), `pathSegments: [id]`. Implemented and tested; no call
53	  site in this unit's UI flow (research.md R7).
54	- Both retry exactly once through `SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure` before giving up
55	  (research.md R4) — see `contracts/entries-repository-extension.md` for the exact sequence. `create()` is
56	  untouched.

62	objects) — no duplicated parsing logic. `list()` additionally parses `meta.nextCursor`.

71	
72	```dart
73	Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
74	  String function, {

86	## `SyncBadgeState` / `LocalWriteOutcome` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`) — NEW
87	
88	```dart
89	enum SyncBadgeState { synchronized, synchronizing, error }
90	enum LocalWriteOutcome { pending, failed }
91	
92	class SyncBadge {
93	  const SyncBadge._();
94	  static SyncBadgeState derive(LocalWriteOutcome? localWrite) => switch (localWrite) {
95	    null => SyncBadgeState.synchronized,
96	    LocalWriteOutcome.pending => SyncBadgeState.synchronizing,
97	    LocalWriteOutcome.failed => SyncBadgeState.error,
98	  };
99	}
100	```
101	
102	A pure, total function over `sync-badge.md`'s model (research.md R6). `RecordsBloc` calls it with
103	`localWrite: null` for every entry it ever renders — both of its entry sources (`EntriesRepository.list()`'s
104	results, `.cachedEntries`) are, by construction, already server-confirmed. Never depends on session/auth state
105	(FR-005), by having no session-related input at all.
106	
107	**Mapping to the prototype's sync badge** (`prototype-extract.md` §3/§6 — reuses existing `DesignTokens`
108	verbatim, no new token):
109	
110	| `SyncBadgeState` | Dot color | Label |
111	|---|---|---|
112	| `synchronized` | `DesignTokens.colorSuccess` (`#4C6B4F`) | "sincronizado" |
113	| `synchronizing` | `DesignTokens.colorWarningSync` (`#C98A3E`) | "sincronizando" |
114	| `error` | `DesignTokens.colorError` (`#B3402A`) | "erro de sync" |
115	
116	## `DateGroup` / `DateGrouper` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/date_group.dart`) — NEW
117	
118	Maps spec.md's "Entry Timeline Page" grouping requirement (FR-002) to a pure function, independent of widget
119	code so it's directly unit-testable (RNF07).
120	
121	```dart
122	class DateGroup extends Equatable {
123	  const DateGroup({required this.label, required this.entries});
124	  final String label;            // "Hoje" | "Ontem" | "{day} de {monthName}" (research.md R9)
125	  final List<Entry> entries;     // newest-to-oldest by occurredAt (resolved ordering Clarification)
126	}
127	
128	class DateGrouper {
129	  const DateGrouper._();
130	  static List<DateGroup> group(List<Entry> entries, {DateTime? now});
131	}
132	```
133	
134	- Input `entries` is assumed already sorted newest-to-oldest (see `EntryMerger` below, which guarantees this
135	  for `RecordsBloc`'s own data) — `group()` only buckets, it never re-sorts within or across groups.
136	  Groups themselves come out newest-to-oldest because the input is.
137	- Bucketing compares each entry's `occurredAt.toLocal()` calendar day against `(now ?? DateTime.now()).toLocal()`'s —
138	  the device's local calendar day (spec.md Assumptions), not UTC.
139	- `now` is an optional override purely for deterministic unit tests ("today" fixed at a known instant); production call sites omit it.
140	
141	## `EntryMerger` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/entry_merger.dart`) — NEW
142	
143	Implements spec.md's resolved Clarification 3 (dedupe-by-ID, preferring the fresher copy).
144	
145	```dart
146	class EntryMerger {
147	  const EntryMerger._();
148	  static List<Entry> merge({required List<Entry> primary, required List<Entry> secondary}) {
149	    // union by id, primary's copy wins on a shared id, result sorted newest-to-oldest by occurredAt
150	  }
151	}
152	```
153	
154	`RecordsBloc` calls `EntryMerger.merge(primary: <freshly fetched or already-displayed entries>, secondary:
155	entriesRepository.cachedEntries)` every time it has a new batch to show (research.md R3) — never inside
156	`EntriesRepositoryImpl`.
157	
158	## `RecordsEvent` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_event.dart`) — NEW
159	
160	| Event | When |
161	|---|---|
162	| `RecordsStarted` | `RecordsPage.initState` — triggers the first page fetch. |
163	| `NextPageRequested` | The list's `ScrollController` crosses a near-bottom threshold, and `!hasReachedEnd && !isLoadingMore`. |
164	| `PageLoadRetried` | The user taps "Tentar novamente" on a failed first load (`RecordsLoadFailure`) or a failed further-page load (`RecordsLoaded.pageLoadFailure`). |
165	| `RecordsLocalCacheRefreshed` | `RecordsPage`, once the insertion-modal `showModalBottomSheet` future resolves (research.md R10) — re-merges `cachedEntries` into the currently displayed list, no network call. |
166	
167	## `RecordsState` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_state.dart`) — NEW
168	
169	Maps spec.md's "Entry Timeline Page" key entity directly to this sealed state's `RecordsLoaded` fields
170	(entries fetched so far + the cursor to continue from) — no separate domain class for it (research.md-style
171	reasonable decision: nothing else needs this shape outside the bloc that owns it).
172	
173	```dart
174	sealed class RecordsState {}
175	
176	class RecordsLoading extends RecordsState {}
177	
178	class RecordsLoadFailure extends RecordsState {
179	  const RecordsLoadFailure(this.failure);
180	  final Failure failure;   // any failure type, including AuthExpiredFailure (research.md — see below)
181	}
182	
183	class RecordsLoaded extends RecordsState {
184	  const RecordsLoaded({
185	    required this.entries,        // merged + deduped, newest-to-oldest
186	    required this.nextCursor,
187	    required this.isLoadingMore,
188	    this.pageLoadFailure,         // a further-page fetch failed; entries above stay intact, retryable
189	  });
190	  final List<Entry> entries;
191	  final String? nextCursor;
192	  final bool isLoadingMore;
193	  final Failure? pageLoadFailure;
194	
195	  bool get hasReachedEnd => nextCursor == null;
196	  bool get isEmpty => entries.isEmpty;   // RecordsPage renders "Vazio" for this, never a separate event
197	}
198	```
199	
200	- **First-load failure, any cause (including `AuthExpiredFailure`)** → `RecordsLoadFailure` — never the empty
201	  state, so a true zero-entries account is never confused with "couldn't load" (research.md's reasoning under
202	  R5/R7). The one-shot `reauthRequired` stream (next section) still fires in the `AuthExpiredFailure` case, on
203	  top of this state — the overlay appears over the retryable error screen.
204	- **Further-page failure, `AuthExpiredFailure`** → `entries`/`nextCursor` are left exactly as they were,
205	  `isLoadingMore` resets to `false` (so the next scroll-near-bottom re-attempts the same, unconsumed cursor);
206	  `pageLoadFailure` is **not** set for this case — only the one-shot stream fires. This is what makes FR-007's
207	  "without discarding the entries already loaded or the current scroll position... restored exactly as it
208	  was" true by construction (nothing in `RecordsState` changed).
209	- **Further-page failure, any other cause** (timeout, offline, validation, ...) → `pageLoadFailure` set,
210	  `isLoadingMore` resets to `false`, entries unchanged — a retryable inline banner at the bottom of the list
211	  (FR-009/Edge Cases).
212	
213	## `RecordsBloc` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_bloc.dart`) — NEW
214	
215	```dart
216	class RecordsBloc extends Bloc<RecordsEvent, RecordsState> {
217	  RecordsBloc({required EntriesRepository entriesRepository});
218	
219	  Stream<void> get reauthRequired;   // one-shot (research.md R5) — fired on a post-retry AuthExpiredFailure
220	}
221	```
222	
223	Depends only on `EntriesRepository` (never `SessionRepository`, never `ConnectivityChecker` — research.md
224	R4/R11) — the one domain-layer dependency this bloc needs. Never imports `SessionBloc` or any of its
225	event/state types (requirements.md RF07's own acceptance criterion).
226

230	
231	- `records_page.dart` — `Scaffold` with the prototype's header (back arrow, title, inert download icon —
232	  FR-008), inert search bar + funnel button (FR-008), a `ListView` driven by `RecordsLoaded.entries` grouped
233	  through `DateGrouper`, a `ScrollController` that survives `BlocBuilder` rebuilds (never recreated, so scroll
234	  position is never lost — FR-003/FR-007), and the `reauthRequired` subscription (research.md R5).
235	- `record_card.dart` — one entry: spine + icon colored by `source` (table below), monospace time
236	  (`occurredAt.toLocal()`, `HH:mm`), `SyncBadgeDot` (table above), text excerpt (`content`, no truncation logic
237	  beyond what the card's fixed layout naturally clips), tag chips (`EntryTag.name`, only when `tags.isNotEmpty`
238	  — FR-002/Acceptance Scenario 2).
239	- `records_empty_state.dart` — notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", "Criar primeiro registro" button
240	  calling the shared `openInsertionModal()` (research.md R10).
241	- `sync_badge_dot.dart` — the 8px dot + mono label pair, parameterized by `SyncBadgeState`.
242	
243	**Origin marker mapping** (`prototype-extract.md`'s `sourceMeta`, verbatim hex — reuses existing `DesignTokens`,
244	no new color token; Phosphor icon names mapped to this app's existing Material-icon convention, same mapping
245	style RF01/RF02 already used for their own icons):
246	
247	| `EntrySource` | Spine/icon color | Material icon (Phosphor equivalent) |
248	|---|---|---|
249	| `manual` | `DesignTokens.colorPrimary` (`#1F3D34`) | `Icons.edit_outlined` (`ph-pencil-simple`) |
250	| `audio` | `DesignTokens.colorSecondary` (`#7C8B6F`) | `Icons.mic_none` (`ph-microphone`) |
251	| `photo` | `DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary` (`#6B6255`) | `Icons.image_outlined` (`ph-image`) |
252	| `chat` | `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (`#C98A3E`) | `Icons.chat_bubble_outline` (`ph-chat-circle-text`) |
253	
254	## Routing / DI changes
255	
256	- `lib/core/routing/app_router.dart`: `AppRoutes.records`'s builder wraps `RecordsPage` in
257	  `BlocProvider<RecordsBloc>(create: (_) => getIt<RecordsBloc>()..add(const RecordsStarted()))`, replacing the
258	  direct `RecordsPlaceholderPage()` builder. `records_placeholder_page.dart` is deleted.
259	- `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`: `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s registration gains `sessionRepository:
260	  getIt<SessionRepository>()`; one new `getIt.registerFactory<RecordsBloc>(...)`.

```dart
  Map<String, dynamic>? body,
  List<String>? pathSegments,
  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,   // NEW (research.md R1)
  AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession,
})
```

`queryParameters` is passed straight through to `Dio.request()`. Every existing call site (`entries-create`,
`auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) is unaffected — the parameter defaults to omitted.

## `SyncBadgeState` / `LocalWriteOutcome` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`) — NEW

```dart
enum SyncBadgeState { synchronized, synchronizing, error }
enum LocalWriteOutcome { pending, failed }

class SyncBadge {
  const SyncBadge._();
  static SyncBadgeState derive(LocalWriteOutcome? localWrite) => switch (localWrite) {
    null => SyncBadgeState.synchronized,
    LocalWriteOutcome.pending => SyncBadgeState.synchronizing,
    LocalWriteOutcome.failed => SyncBadgeState.error,
  };
}
```

A pure, total function over `sync-badge.md`'s model (research.md R6). `RecordsBloc` calls it with
`localWrite: null` for every entry it ever renders — both of its entry sources (`EntriesRepository.list()`'s
results, `.cachedEntries`) are, by construction, already server-confirmed. Never depends on session/auth state
(FR-005), by having no session-related input at all.

**Mapping to the prototype's sync badge** (`prototype-extract.md` §3/§6 — reuses existing `DesignTokens`
verbatim, no new token):

| `SyncBadgeState` | Dot color | Label |
|---|---|---|
| `synchronized` | `DesignTokens.colorSuccess` (`#4C6B4F`) | "sincronizado" |
| `synchronizing` | `DesignTokens.colorWarningSync` (`#C98A3E`) | "sincronizando" |
| `error` | `DesignTokens.colorError` (`#B3402A`) | "erro de sync" |

## `DateGroup` / `DateGrouper` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/date_group.dart`) — NEW

Maps spec.md's "Entry Timeline Page" grouping requirement (FR-002) to a pure function, independent of widget
code so it's directly unit-testable (RNF07).

```dart
class DateGroup extends Equatable {
  const DateGroup({required this.label, required this.entries});
  final String label;            // "Hoje" | "Ontem" | "{day} de {monthName}" (research.md R9)
  final List<Entry> entries;     // newest-to-oldest by occurredAt (resolved ordering Clarification)
}

class DateGrouper {
  const DateGrouper._();
  static List<DateGroup> group(List<Entry> entries, {DateTime? now});
}
```

- Input `entries` is assumed already sorted newest-to-oldest (see `EntryMerger` below, which guarantees this
  for `RecordsBloc`'s own data) — `group()` only buckets, it never re-sorts within or across groups.
  Groups themselves come out newest-to-oldest because the input is.
- Bucketing compares each entry's `occurredAt.toLocal()` calendar day against `(now ?? DateTime.now()).toLocal()`'s —
  the device's local calendar day (spec.md Assumptions), not UTC.
- `now` is an optional override purely for deterministic unit tests ("today" fixed at a known instant); production call sites omit it.

## `EntryMerger` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/entry_merger.dart`) — NEW

Implements spec.md's resolved Clarification 3 (dedupe-by-ID, preferring the fresher copy).

```dart
class EntryMerger {
  const EntryMerger._();
  static List<Entry> merge({required List<Entry> primary, required List<Entry> secondary}) {
    // union by id, primary's copy wins on a shared id, result sorted newest-to-oldest by occurredAt
  }
}
```

`RecordsBloc` calls `EntryMerger.merge(primary: <freshly fetched or already-displayed entries>, secondary:
entriesRepository.cachedEntries)` every time it has a new batch to show (research.md R3) — never inside
`EntriesRepositoryImpl`.

## `RecordsEvent` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_event.dart`) — NEW

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `RecordsStarted` | `RecordsPage.initState` — triggers the first page fetch. |
| `NextPageRequested` | The list's `ScrollController` crosses a near-bottom threshold, and `!hasReachedEnd && !isLoadingMore`. |
| `PageLoadRetried` | The user taps "Tentar novamente" on a failed first load (`RecordsLoadFailure`) or a failed further-page load (`RecordsLoaded.pageLoadFailure`). |
| `RecordsLocalCacheRefreshed` | `RecordsPage`, once the insertion-modal `showModalBottomSheet` future resolves (research.md R10) — re-merges `cachedEntries` into the currently displayed list, no network call. |

## `RecordsState` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_state.dart`) — NEW

Maps spec.md's "Entry Timeline Page" key entity directly to this sealed state's `RecordsLoaded` fields
(entries fetched so far + the cursor to continue from) — no separate domain class for it (research.md-style
reasonable decision: nothing else needs this shape outside the bloc that owns it).

```dart
sealed class RecordsState {}

class RecordsLoading extends RecordsState {}

class RecordsLoadFailure extends RecordsState {
  const RecordsLoadFailure(this.failure);
  final Failure failure;   // any failure type, including AuthExpiredFailure (research.md — see below)
}

class RecordsLoaded extends RecordsState {
  const RecordsLoaded({
    required this.entries,        // merged + deduped, newest-to-oldest
    required this.nextCursor,
    required this.isLoadingMore,
    this.pageLoadFailure,         // a further-page fetch failed; entries above stay intact, retryable
  });
  final List<Entry> entries;
  final String? nextCursor;
  final bool isLoadingMore;
  final Failure? pageLoadFailure;

  bool get hasReachedEnd => nextCursor == null;
  bool get isEmpty => entries.isEmpty;   // RecordsPage renders "Vazio" for this, never a separate event
}
```

- **First-load failure, any cause (including `AuthExpiredFailure`)** → `RecordsLoadFailure` — never the empty
  state, so a true zero-entries account is never confused with "couldn't load" (research.md's reasoning under
  R5/R7). The one-shot `reauthRequired` stream (next section) still fires in the `AuthExpiredFailure` case, on
  top of this state — the overlay appears over the retryable error screen.
- **Further-page failure, `AuthExpiredFailure`** → `entries`/`nextCursor` are left exactly as they were,
  `isLoadingMore` resets to `false` (so the next scroll-near-bottom re-attempts the same, unconsumed cursor);
  `pageLoadFailure` is **not** set for this case — only the one-shot stream fires. This is what makes FR-007's
  "without discarding the entries already loaded or the current scroll position... restored exactly as it
  was" true by construction (nothing in `RecordsState` changed).
- **Further-page failure, any other cause** (timeout, offline, validation, ...) → `pageLoadFailure` set,
  `isLoadingMore` resets to `false`, entries unchanged — a retryable inline banner at the bottom of the list
  (FR-009/Edge Cases).

## `RecordsBloc` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_bloc.dart`) — NEW

```dart
class RecordsBloc extends Bloc<RecordsEvent, RecordsState> {
  RecordsBloc({required EntriesRepository entriesRepository});

  Stream<void> get reauthRequired;   // one-shot (research.md R5) — fired on a post-retry AuthExpiredFailure
}
```

Depends only on `EntriesRepository` (never `SessionRepository`, never `ConnectivityChecker` — research.md
R4/R11) — the one domain-layer dependency this bloc needs. Never imports `SessionBloc` or any of its
event/state types (requirements.md RF07's own acceptance criterion).

| `chat` | `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (`#C98A3E`) | `Icons.chat_bubble_outline` (`ph-chat-circle-text`) |

            in_domain = '/domain/' in line

            if int(parts[1]) > 0:

            total_lines += 1

                hit_lines += 1
print(f"domain lines: {total_lines}, hit: {hit_lines}, pct: {100*hit_lines/total_lines:.2f}%")

# Quickstart: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)

How to validate this unit end-to-end once implemented, mapped to spec.md's four user stories. A run guide —
interfaces are in `contracts/`, state/entities in `data-model.md`.

## Prerequisites

- F000, RF01, RF03 already implemented and passing (this unit depends on all three per spec.md's header).
  `EntriesRepository`/`Entry`/`CreateEntryUseCase` (RF01) and `SessionRepository`/`SessionBloc`/the "Sessão
  expirada" overlay (F000) are extended, not replaced.
- A signed-in test account with entries spanning at least 3 different calendar days, created across at least
  `manual`, `audio`, and `photo` origins (reuse RF01/RF02's own fixtures to create them), and — since no
  capture flow can produce one — a `chat`-sourced entry seeded directly in the backend/fixtures to exercise
  Edge Cases' "renders a `chat` entry without erroring" scenario.
- A second, brand-new test account with zero entries, for Story 2.
- Enough entries (more than one backend page — the default page size is 20) to exercise pagination for
  Story 1's Acceptance Scenario 3.

## Automated checks

```bash
fvm flutter analyze                                    # RNF06 import-shape lint
fvm flutter test --coverage
lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info
genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain-html    # RNF07 gate — now covering entry_merger.dart,
                                                         # date_group.dart, sync_badge_state.dart, plus
                                                         # EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()/getById()
dart test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart   # requirements.md RF07's own acceptance criterion
```

`contracts/entries-repository-extension.md` and `contracts/records-bloc.md` each carry the full scenario
table this unit's coverage depends on.

## Manual verification (device/Simulator)

### Story 1 — Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of origin (P1)

1. Open the side menu (☰) → "Meus Registros" from Home/Chat. **Expect**: records grouped under "Hoje" /
   "Ontem" / explicit older dates (newest group first), each card showing the right spine color + icon for
   its origin (manual = dark green/pencil, audio = olive green/mic, photo = gray/image, chat =
   ochre/chat-bubble), a time, a sync badge, a text excerpt, and tag chips only on entries that actually have
   tags.
2. Confirm the seeded `chat`-origin entry renders like any other card (ochre spine, chat-bubble icon) — no
   crash, no "unrecognized" placeholder.
3. Scroll to the bottom. **Expect**: further entries load and append automatically, with no "load more"
   button, no disturbance to the cards already on screen, and no visible scroll jump.
4. Scroll to the true end of history. **Expect**: loading simply stops — no error banner, no "end of list"
   message.

### Story 2 — Starting from nothing (P1)

1. Sign in on the zero-entries account, open "Meus Registros". **Expect**: the notebook icon, "Nenhum
   registro ainda", and the "Criar primeiro registro" button — never a blank or perpetually-loading screen.
2. Tap "Criar primeiro registro". **Expect**: the same Insertion Modal RF01/RF02 already built opens over
   this screen.
3. Save a text entry. **Expect**: the modal closes back onto "Meus Registros" (not Home/Chat), and the new
   entry now appears in its correct date group ("Hoje"), replacing the empty state.

### Story 3 — The session expires while browsing (P2)

1. Load "Meus Registros" with several entries visible, scroll to a specific, identifiable position.
2. Force the next `GET /entries` call to return `AUTH_EXPIRED` (e.g., via a debug toggle/expired test token)
   and either scroll further or wait for a background refresh attempt to trigger it. **Expect**: the "Sessão
   expirada" overlay appears over the screen; the entries and scroll position underneath are completely
   unchanged (confirm by dismissing-and-checking before re-authenticating, if your test harness allows it).
3. Tap "Entrar novamente" and re-authenticate successfully. **Expect**: the overlay dismisses; the screen is
   exactly as it was (same entries, same scroll position) — no reload, no reordering.
4. Scroll further again. **Expect**: pagination now resumes normally (the next page is fetched successfully
   with the fresh session).

### Story 4 — The sync badge tells the truth, even during session trouble (P3)

1. With entries visible, force a silent session renewal in the background (a renewable `AUTH_EXPIRED` the
   refresh call recovers from transparently). **Expect**: no visible change to any card — no badge flicker,
   no overlay, no reload (silent renewal never surfaces to the UI).
2. Repeat Story 3's forced-expiry-and-overlay flow. **Expect**: once the overlay is dismissed, every badge on
   every card underneath shows exactly the same state (color + label) it showed before the overlay appeared.
3. Since every entry this unit can display is already server-confirmed by construction (research.md R6),
   every badge observed in steps 1–2 should read "sincronizado" (green) — this is expected, not a bug; it is
   not possible to observe "sincronizando"/"erro de sync" through this unit's own flows alone (spec.md
   Assumptions).

### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once

- Turn on airplane mode after the first page has loaded, then scroll to trigger another page. **Expect**: a
  clear, retryable inline error at the bottom of the list; the entries already shown stay visible and
  scrollable; no write of any kind is attempted.
- Turn airplane mode back on, tap the retry affordance from that error. **Expect**: it fails again cleanly
  (no crash); turn airplane mode off and retry again. **Expect**: pagination resumes normally.
- Force the very first `GET /entries` call (on screen open) to fail outright (not just offline). **Expect**:
  a full-screen retryable error — never the "Nenhum registro ainda" empty state.
- Tap the header's download icon and the search bar/funnel button. **Expect**: both render exactly per the
  prototype but do nothing (FR-008 — inert placeholders; no export, no filter sheet, no search).
- With a known seeded account (more than one page of entries where the newest page happens to be empty, e.g.
  nothing created "today" or "yesterday" but older entries exist), open "Meus Registros". **Expect**: paging
  continues directly to the older groups — the empty state must **not** appear.
